record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Conservation laws for non-Benenti elements of K(V)
record.original_question: For a non-Benenti, generically bad element K in K(V), is V the only conservation law for K, or does K admit many conservation laws, and if so how can those conservation laws be described?

evidence.quote: Q7 Again about known examples. Take K ∈ K(V ) which is not Benenti but, on the contrary, is a ‘bad’ generic element of K(V ). We know that V is a conservation law for K. Does K admit any other conservation laws, or V is unique? If K admits ‘many’ conservation laws, what can we say about them?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let M be a smooth manifold and let L: TM → TM be a (1,1)-tensor field whose Nijenhuis torsion

  N_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] − L[LX,Y] − L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]

vanishes identically; such an L is called a Nijenhuis operator. A function f ∈ C^∞(M) is called a conservation law of L if the 1-form L^* df is closed, i.e. d(L^* df) = 0. Given a Nijenhuis operator L, denote by K(L) the (real) vector space

  K(L) := { K: TM → TM (1,1)-tensor : N_{L+tK} ≡ 0 for all t ∈ ℝ, i.e. K is Nijenhuis-compatible with L },

equivalently the space of operators K such that L and K have vanishing mutual Nijenhuis torsion. For a fixed Nijenhuis operator V ∈ K(V) (so that V itself plays the role of the base element and K(V) is the space of operators compatible with V), one says that V is a conservation law for K ∈ K(V) in the sense that the trace coefficients of V provide closed 1-forms under K^*.

An element K ∈ K(V) is called Benenti-type if it is generated by V in a polynomial / standard fashion (so that conservation laws are inherited from V in a controlled way). Call K ∈ K(V) generically bad (non-Benenti) if at a generic point of M the algebraic type of K does not match the structure produced by Benenti-type elements of K(V), so that the standard mechanism for producing conservation laws from V fails.

Problem. Let V be a Nijenhuis operator on M and let K ∈ K(V) be a non-Benenti, generically bad element. It is known that V is a conservation law for K. Determine whether V is the only conservation law of K (up to the obvious functional dependencies), or whether K admits additional, functionally independent conservation laws. In the latter case, give a description of the space of all conservation laws of such a K — for instance, by characterising their construction, their functional dimension, or their dependence on V and on the algebraic invariants of K.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research problem in the recent survey on Nijenhuis geometry and integrable systems. Related literature (e.g. work on conservation laws and symmetries of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators, and on Benenti systems) addresses the Benenti / regular case but does not resolve the case of non-Benenti, generically bad elements of K(V). No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry IV: conservation laws, symmetries and integration of certain non-diagonalisable systems of hydrodynamic type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies conservation laws and symmetries of gl-regular Nijenhuis operators.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results cover regular/Benenti-type situations but not the non-Benenti generically bad case.
